facts.about: Avenue Supermarts Limited (DMart) is a national supermarket chain, with a focus on value-retailing. We offer a wide range of products with a focus on the Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG) and General Merchandise & Apparel product categories.

flags.text: Profit compounding (+8%/yr) lags sales (+17%/yr) over 3 years — margins under pressure
Cash-rich profits: 5-yr operating cash = 105% of PAT

business.summary: Avenue Supermarts Ltd. (DMart) is a national supermarket chain focused on value-retailing. It offers a wide range of products across Foods, Non-Foods (FMCG), and General Merchandise & Apparel, operating under an 'Everyday Low Cost/Everyday Low Price' model.

guidance.statement: Internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base annually.
guidance.quote: So I do want to state that internally, our benchmarks will remain that we should be opening around 15% of our store base as the number that we want to increase annually.

guidance.statement: We believe that a 15% gross margin and around a 5% net margin should be the North Star.
guidance.quote: And so therefore, 15% kind of a gross margin and let's say around a 5% kind of a net margin should be the North Star for this business even in the future.

guidance.statement: We hope to continue acceleration and open more stores than in the past.
guidance.quote: We have opened 50 stores last year and we hope to continue the acceleration and actually try and open as many more than we have opened in the past.

guidance.statement: Store additions will not be less than 50 next year.
guidance.quote: I mean, it won't be less than 50. I mean, if you're talking so much about it.

guidance.statement: DMart Ready is a business that can be broken even in a couple of years.
guidance.quote: So, I can't give any forward-looking points of view on when will it be profitable or breakeven or all that. But broadly, we feel that this is a business that can be broken even in a couple of years.

guidance.statement: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores.
guidance.quote: We are primed and ready in terms of opening around 40-50 stores.

guidance.statement: You can take a range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.
guidance.quote: So, you can take a range of 40 to 60 over the next three years.

scorecard.promised: 40-50 stores in FY25; range of 40-60 over three years.
scorecard.delivered: Revenue hit ₹59,358 cr in Mar 2025 (+16.9% YoY) as store network expanded.
scorecard.evidence: FY25 revenue grew to ₹59,358 cr from ₹50,789 cr in FY24, supporting physical store footprint expansion.

scorecard.promised: Store additions will not be less than 50 next year (FY26).
scorecard.delivered: Mar 2026 revenue reached ₹68,821 cr; quarterly revenue grew 14.9% YoY in Jun 2026.
scorecard.evidence: Full year FY26 revenue reached ₹68,821 cr (+15.9% YoY), supported by continued new store additions.

scorecard.promised: Internally benchmark to open around 15% of store base annually in FY27.
scorecard.delivered: Sep 2026 quarterly revenue hit ₹19,644 cr (+17.8% YoY).
scorecard.evidence: Requires sustained addition of ~15% to store base in FY27; Q2 FY27 revenue stands at ₹19,644 cr.

scorecard.promised: Aim for a 15% gross margin and around 5% net margin as North Star.
scorecard.delivered: Operating margin was 8% in FY26; Net Profit was ₹2,970 cr on ₹68,821 cr revenue (~4.3% net margin).
scorecard.evidence: FY26 PAT margin was ~4.31% (₹2,970 cr / ₹68,821 cr), remaining below the 5% net margin target.

scorecard.promised: DMart Ready can be broken even in a couple of years.
scorecard.delivered: Avenue E-Commerce Limited subsidiary continues to post ongoing losses.
scorecard.evidence: Annual report risks note subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce Limited has continued losses, requiring ongoing evaluation.

narrative.scoreline: DMart consistently delivers high double-digit revenue growth via store additions, but operating margins remain locked at 8%, keeping profit growth below top-line expansion.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Blended gross margins are expected to remain in the 14.5% to 15.5% range.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Operating margins have hovered predictably between 7% and 8% across FY25–FY27 quarters.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: General merchandise and apparel run rates will remain around 23%.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Full-year operating margins remained steady at 8% in FY25 and FY26.

narrativeVsNumbers.claim: Quick commerce has a negligible 1% to 1.5% impact with no red flags.
narrativeVsNumbers.reality: Revenue YoY growth moderated from 17.7% in Dec 2024 to 13.3% in Dec 2025 before recovering.

bull: Revenue compounded strongly from ₹50,789 cr in FY24 to ₹68,821 cr in FY26.
Operating cash flow reached ₹3,467 cr in FY26, covering 116% of Net Profit.
Balance sheet remains conservative with a low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.16×.
bear: 3-year profit compounding of +8%/yr lags revenue growth of +17%/yr due to margin caps.
Free cash flow was negative at -₹646 cr in FY26 due to high ongoing store capex.
Avenue E-Commerce Limited continues to run operating losses, dragging on overall profitability.
watch: Check if Q3 FY27 PAT margin moves closer to the 5% North Star target.

claims.claim: We are focusing on 11 key cities to prove a sustainable, profitable e-commerce model with six-hour delivery.
claims.quote: We made a conscious choice to double down on DMart Ready in 11 key cities where the vast majority of our online business comes from. We want our team to be laser-focused on proving that we can run a truly sustainable, profitable e-commerce model here.

claims.claim: We are not identifying markets solely based on quick commerce presence; we look at density and strategic opportunities.
claims.quote: So, it's not as if we are now identifying those markets where quick commerce is not present and hence only opening there. That is not the strategy at all.

claims.claim: SSSG for older stores is expected to hover at current levels due to maturity and high density.
claims.quote: And so therefore, same-store growth would possibly be hovering more in the range that we are seeing today, and we are not likely to see that go up considerably, all things being constant.

claims.claim: We follow the 20-20-20 principle, focusing on value, margin, and volume share, without a conscious effort to drive shelf space.
claims.quote: So I would only say that there is no such conscious effort to try and drive shelf space. A lot of what you see on the shelf in DMart is driven more by customer choice.

claims.claim: The right method of expansion is to open 10% to 20% of base stores every year.
claims.quote: Like we have always said that the right method of expansion in the offline space is to open on an average every year at least 10% to 15% or maybe 10% to 20% of your base stores – every year.

claims.claim: Deflation in staples results in a huge volume pickup as shoppers substitute categories.
claims.quote: So, whenever there is a deflation, you get huge volume pickup in those categories. Because people buy more of that and substitute something else.

claims.claim: Private labels follow a 20-20-20 principle for share, price discount, and margin advantage.
claims.quote: The broad principle is we follow a 20-20-20 principle. The 20-20-20 principle is, first and foremost, do we have an opportunity to at least gain a 20% share?

claims.claim: General merchandise and apparel contribution will remain around the current run rates of around 23%.
claims.quote: A broad trend line will be around the current run rates of around 23%, is the sense we get.

claims.claim: DMart Ready is focused on consolidation and high throughputs in existing cities rather than fast expansion.
claims.quote: this year would be a year of consolidation and we'll try and test whatever we have done and hence, we added just one city.

claims.claim: Quick commerce is having a negligible 1% to 1.5% SSSG CAGR impact on metro stores.
claims.quote: maybe 1%-1.5% kind of an impact could be there. But is any of my store declining, negative? Do I see very large red flags? Absolutely not.

claims.claim: Blended gross margins are expected to remain in the 14.5% to 15.5% range.
claims.quote: I think 14.5%, 15%, 15.5%, those are the kind of ranges we play in from a gross margin standpoint.

claims.claim: 29% of store cohorts are in towns with a population of less than 5 lakhs.
claims.quote: we have got 1% better in less than 5 lakh town population, we were at 28% of the store cohorts in FY '23, it's become 29%.

risks.text: Competitive intensity and inability to maintain EDLC/EDLP pricing strategy could adversely affect business and operations.
Availability of commercially viable real estate properties at suitable locations for new stores.
Climate change may result in lower sales, lesser profits, and increased investments in the short-term.
Material related party transactions with subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce Limited require member approval.
Subsidiary Avenue E-Commerce Limited has continued losses, indicating potential impairment in investment value.
